title: The Whistleblower Link: Mapping Where Internal Safety Concerns Fail to Reach Regulators

original_idea.body:
# The Whistleblower Link: Mapping Where Internal Safety Concerns Fail to Reach Regulators

**Problem:** Internal-accountability chain: 'employee observes a safety problem' -> 'safe channel exists to report' -> 'report reaches an external regulator' -> 'regulator can act'. SB 53 adds whistleblower protections, but whether a usable channel-to-regulator link actually exists across labs is undocumented.

**Direction:** Survey the publicly documented internal reporting channels and whistleblower provisions of frontier labs and relevant laws (SB 53, EU mechanisms), coding each on whether a concern can reach an external body without lab gatekeeping. Identify the precise link where the only available path routes back through the employer.

**Why it matters:** Whistleblowing is often the last detection mechanism for risks labs choose not to disclose. Showing where the reporting chain dead-ends inside the company highlights the missing external-channel link that governance must build. Pure document/legal analysis, no compute, counterfactual.

**Relevant context:** California SB 53 'Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act' (whistleblower protections, critical safety incident reporting); EU AI Office notification commitments; FLI AI Safety Index information-sharing domain.
